title: File names, archive members, and decoders acting on untrusted bytes

threat_model.actor: Anyone who can supply a file, a file name, an archive, or bytes that a later process decodes, including through an import, a queue, a shared bucket, or a cache
threat_model.asset: The storage layout the application relies on and the process that interprets the bytes it reads back
threat_model.trust_boundary: The name or bytes as supplied and the path finally written or the object graph finally constructed
threat_model.failure_mode: Containment is asserted on a string rather than on the resolved path, or a decoder that can construct arbitrary objects is reached by bytes the process never authenticated
threat_model.impact: A write lands outside the intended directory, or a decoder builds objects of the attacker's choosing and executes code inside the worker

required_evidence: The application accepts, stores, extracts, or serves files whose names or contents originate outside the codebase
A path is composed, an archive is expanded, or bytes are decoded into objects on a path a caller can influence

signals: Containment is checked with a string prefix comparison rather than a path-component comparison
The traversal check runs before a decode, normalization, or join that can reintroduce a separator
A directory is created from the composed path before that path has been validated
Member names are validated but link members are still materialised
The size budget is taken from the archive header rather than from the bytes actually written
A nested archive is expanded by a second helper that repeats none of the outer checks
A decoder that can construct arbitrary types is applied to bytes from a cache, a queue, a cookie, or a request
An integrity tag is optional, so an entry that omits it takes an unauthenticated branch
The integrity comparison runs after the decode, or covers a key rather than the payload
The type is taken from the declared header or the extension rather than from the bytes
Uploaded content is served from the application origin with a caller-influenced content type
A parser resolves external entities, remote subresources, or nested documents on its own
An extractor asserts containment with a string prefix against a destination that has no trailing separator
A cache codec treats a missing integrity tag as a legacy exemption and decodes anyway

boundary.subject: the storage root and the process that decodes what it reads
boundary.object: the path finally written or served, and the object graph the decoder constructs
boundary.invariant: Every write resolves inside the intended root as a whole path component, and every decoder that can construct objects is reached only by bytes the process authenticated

examples: Upload saved under a composed path
Temporary file created from a supplied name
Template or asset resolved from a request path
Native object deserialization of cached bytes
Signed cookie or token payload decoding
XML or spreadsheet parsing with entity resolution
Uploaded file served from the application origin
Content type derived from the supplied name

signals: Trace the name from the entrypoint to the write and note every decode, join, normalization, and rename between them
Compare the string the containment check examines with the path the write actually uses
Find every decoder call and establish, for each, which branches can reach it without an integrity check
State the storage root as a path and confirm the check compares components rather than string prefixes
Decide whether the decoder is required to be reachable at all, and whether a safer format would carry the same payload
Establish whether size, entry count, and nesting budgets are enforced against produced bytes rather than declared ones
Identify who can write into the store, cache, or queue that the decoder later reads
Establish whether stored names are reused later for serving, linking, or re-import
Run the extraction into a disposable temporary root and record the resolved path of every entry written
Exercise the containment helper alone on encoded, nested, absolute, and sibling-prefix names and record which it accepts

steps: Confirm explicit authorization and work only inside a disposable temporary directory that holds no real data
Extract or upload a benign control file first, so a later difference is attributable to the crafted input
Craft names that resolve to a sibling of the root rather than to any system location, and record where the write lands
Exercise the decoder path with an entry that omits the integrity tag and record whether it is refused
Record resolved paths, enforced budgets, and the reachable entrypoint without overwriting anything outside the temporary root

false_positive_filters: Containment is asserted on the resolved path with a component-wise comparison, so a sibling prefix cannot pass
The name is reduced to a single component or replaced by a server-generated identifier before any join
The decoder is reached only after a constant-time integrity check over the payload, with no branch that skips it
The store the decoder reads is writable only by the application itself, evidenced by its access configuration rather than assumed from its network position
The parser has entity and subresource resolution disabled, evidenced in its configuration
The suspected path is unreachable from any caller-controlled entrypoint, or belongs to a build-time tool rather than the deployed service

required_evidence: The caller-controlled portion of the name or bytes, and the reachable path to the write or decode
The resolved path the write actually used, or the branch that reached the decoder without authentication
A safe reproduction inside a disposable root that shows the escape or the unauthenticated decode
The defective invariant stated as a containment or authentication failure, with the concrete impact
refutation_tests: Re-check whether the comparison is component-wise, since a correct check and a prefix check look almost identical
Establish the order of decode and validation before asserting an encoded name survives the filter
Determine who can actually write into the store the decoder reads before claiming an unauthenticated decode is reachable
Look for a server-generated name that replaces the supplied one further along the call chain

root_causes: Containment is asserted with a string prefix, so a sibling directory sharing the prefix satisfies it
Validation and use disagree because a decode, join, or normalization happens between them
The extractor materialises link members, so a later write follows a link out of the root
Budgets are taken from attacker-declared header values rather than from bytes actually produced
An integrity tag is optional, so omitting it selects an unauthenticated decode branch
A second expansion or parse path repeats none of the checks the primary path performs

variant_strategy.result_contract: EXACT | VARIANT | REFUTED | BLOCKED; exact and variant matches remain hypotheses until verified

remediation.canonical_invariant: Resolve the path first and assert containment component-wise before any write, and authenticate bytes before any decoder that can construct objects sees them
patterns: Decode and normalize first, then reduce to a single component or a server-generated name, then assert containment on the resolved path
Reject non-regular archive members rather than materialising them, and bound entry count, produced bytes, and nesting depth
Prefer a schema-validated format that constructs only declared types over a decoder that can construct any type
Where a general decoder is genuinely required, authenticate the payload with a constant-time comparison first and leave no branch that skips it
Disable external entity and subresource resolution in document parsers
Serve uploaded content from a separate origin with a server-determined content type and a download disposition

assertions: The vulnerable extractor accepts an entry that resolves to a sibling directory sharing the destination's prefix and creates it on the way
The vulnerable extractor budgets the archive using the declared header size rather than the bytes it writes
The remediated extractor compares whole path components, rejects non-regular members, and counts produced bytes, while still extracting a legitimate archive
The vulnerable codec decodes an entry that omits its integrity tag by taking the legacy branch
The compensated codec keeps the same decoder call yet has no branch reaching it without a constant-time tag comparison over the payload

calibration.notes: This pack has not completed a reproducible benchmark run and makes no precision or recall claim.

limitations: Path semantics differ between platforms and filesystems, so a fixture result on one runtime does not settle behaviour on another
Container filesystem layout, mount options, and process privileges decide what a containment escape is actually worth
Whether an unauthenticated decode is reachable usually depends on who can write to the intervening store, which lives outside the code
Library defaults for entity resolution and archive handling change between versions, so configuration must be read for the version deployed
